articles.title_original: Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders
articles.title_zh: Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders
facts_zh:
Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders
- Published
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, has been found guilty of murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.
Mackenzie ordered members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".
His doctrine said that education was forbidden and modern medicine was "evil".

all_titles.en: Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders

articles.title_original: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support says court filing
articles.title_zh: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support says court filing
facts_zh:
Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support says court filing
- Published
A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according to a court filing, external in California.
US prosecutors claimed Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked for the AI firm, was in "frequent communication...
with a member of the Saudi royal family", and say a member of the country's military paid for a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia for his wife and son after his arrest.

all_titles.en: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support says court filing

articles.title_original: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game
articles.title_zh: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game
facts_zh:
US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game
- Published
A member of the US Air Force died after he fell while abseiling from the ceiling of a Texas stadium ahead of a college football game.

Footage shows the serviceman plummet feet first to the turf midfield at San Antonio's 170ft (52 metre) high Alamodome on Saturday during a ceremony ahead of the game between the University of Texas at San Antonio and the Naval Academy.
The airman, identified, external by the military as Sgt Ian Patterson, a Tactical Air Control Party instructor at Joint Base San Antonio, died in hospital.

articles.title_zh: Meloni calls emergency meeting after weekend of violent clashes
facts_zh:
Meloni calls emergency meeting after weekend of violent clashes
- Published
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is set to hold an emergency security meeting on Monday after protests over the rising cost of living broke out into violent clashes in Milan.
More than 5,000 people gathered over the weekend.
Police deployed tear gas and water cannons after protesters - many in masks - threw paving stones, bins and chairs at officers.

articles.title_zh: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
facts_zh: Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system.
The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore.
However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.

articles.title_original: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
articles.title_zh: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
facts_zh:
Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
- Published
The fire that killed four members of the Canadian military and injured dozens of others on Saturday spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.
It broke out in a grassy training area at a base in the province of Alberta and spread rapidly due to strong winds.
"The fire was 1km (0.6 miles) away when the wind shifted," said Maj-Gen Wade Rutland, commander of the 1st Canadian Division of the Canadian Armed Forces.

articles.title_zh: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
facts_zh: Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand Business live – latest updates Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.
China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday.
The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.

articles.title_original: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
articles.title_zh: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
facts_zh:
Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
- Published
Bangladeshi authorities say they were not informed of the recent execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in the holy city of Mecca until after it had taken place, local media reports.
A Bangladeshi man and woman were executed last Wednesday after being convicted of committing an "indecent act" inside a mosque, according to the Saudi interior ministry.
The ministry did not specify the nature of the offending act.

all_titles.en: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
